subject: Post-call recap: MedTech Inc — Private VPC / Air-gapped constraints
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morris <alex.morris@medtechinc.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@medtechinc.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: MedTech Inc — Private VPC / Air-gapped constraints

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Key business drivers:
- Regulatory / audit requirements: data residency in US and FIPS-compliant key management for PHI workflows.
- Need for an air-gapped or private VPC deployment for model inference to avoid egress of raw data.
- Deterministic latency targets for inference (p95 < 250ms) for clinical triage workflows.

Technical constraints we heard:
- On-prem network is behind a strict outbound proxy and will not allow internet egress from the inference cluster.
- Customer requires integration with their KMS (HSM-backed) and wants to control secrets on-prem.
- Ops team expects audit logs and retention for 2 years; SOC2-type evidence will be required.

Suggested Redwood approach:
- Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) with private control plane option and optional air-gap packaging.
- Use customer-managed KMS for encrypting model artifacts and KV cache.
- Work with your SRE to scope a secure peering/replication plan or an air-gap data transfer process for model updates.

Open questions / next steps:
1) Can you share a high-level network diagram (NAT/proxy details, firewall rules) so our infra team can validate connectivity patterns? (Alex — you mentioned an ops diagram you can send)
2) Who on your security/compliance team should we loop in for SOC2 evidence & KMS architecture reviews?
3) We will draft an SOW for an initial private deployment POC (2 racks equivalent). We aim to share that by EOD Thursday.

Attachments: medtech-network-diagram.png (Alex, if you send this, I will attach to the SOW draft)

Thanks — I’ll coordinate with Marissa (solutions lead) and Dylan (deploy engineering) for a technical review once we have the diagram.

Best,

Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com | (415) 555-0136
Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference

Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: MedTech Inc — Private VPC / Air-gapped constraints

Thanks Camila — this looks right. Attaching the network diagram you asked for (medtech-network-diagram.png). A couple clarifications: 

- Our outbound traffic is limited to a handful of update servers; we would prefer a pull-only model for model updates and have them staged on an internal update mirror.
- KMS is Thales HSM (customer-managed), and we cannot export keys. Any integration needs to support in-place encryption/decryption calls.
- Compliance: our security lead (Priya) will want to review audit log formats and retention policies; she’s on copy.

Next steps on our side:
- Priya will send a short list of required artifacts for your SOC2 evidence review by EOD tomorrow.
- I’ll coordinate with SRE to run through your network checklist and share firewall rules we can open.

Alex

Thanks for the forward. Quick notes from solutions & infra: 

- SOC2 evidence: we can provide SOC2 type II report excerpts, architecture diagrams, and a mapping table for controls. Priya’s list should let us prioritize.
- HSM: Thales is supported via our KMS integration, but we need to validate whether MedTech requires in-VM calls or a network-attached HSM provocation. Dylan — please add specifics.
- Air-gap and update flow: infra confirms a pull-only model update is possible if MedTech hosts an internal mirror with a signed bundle and hash verification. We’ll need the network diagram to finalize the packaging steps.
- Latency: initial sizing for 2 racks with optimized batching looks feasible to target p95 < 250ms for the lightweight triage model; we’ll validate with a microbenchmark during POC.

Next steps I’ll take:
1) Review Priya’s compliance list and prepare a control mapping doc by Monday.
2) Work with legal on a tight SOW that includes audit evidence milestones and acceptance criteria.
3) Help Camila finalize the SOW draft for external review.
